کھلی پیشانی: کانی گرام کے جنوب میں پہاڑی چوٹی کا نام جو درختوں سے خالی ہے "Baar Pit" is the name of the highest point of mountain range facing Kanigram from its south. Baar Pit in Ormuri means "naked forehead" and is rightly so because all area around it is thick wooded except its top when seen from the town across the Badar River. It is the highest and most panoramic mountain peak of the hills surrounding the Kanigram Valley. Behind the Baar Pit peak lies the famous Shughnah Maela beautifu valley wi th Stur Tapar hill standing haughty to its west. Khir Naray crest curves down eastwards between Shughnah Maela and Mashaj Tsappur top wherefrom the historical Mawu Valle y commences its downwards south-eastern journey to meet the Kanigram-wana road near Manda. The Report on Waziristan and its Tribes 1901 has beautifully described it as follows; "Baar Pit" encircles a vast area of the interior of Mahsud country which serves as if it were a second high wall of the mountains. It shuts of Kanigram valley from Khaisora, Shahor, Jandola, and the lower portion of Shi Tak tract. It is connected with Shawal Range by the Sharwangai Kotal between the Khaisora and Kaniguram Valleys. This range may appropriately be termed as the backbone of the country " . Baar Pit is an ideal point where-from one can not only view Kanigram Town and its Valley but also almost all areas around it like Razmak, Ladha, Makin, Shahor, Sararogha, Jandola, Sarvekay, Monzai etc. The distant Gumal Fort ne ar Tank is also visible from here when the weather is clear. End of May is ideal for a clear view of Gumal Bazar and Gumal fort when the weather is usually clear.

Initially the colony was settled by Sheikh Darvesh, nephew of Mian Pir Wali (buried in Kanigram) who migrated from Kanigram at the start of seventeenth century alongwith his followers. The colony was then established in the outskirtsof Jallanghar city but the city has now spread on all sides and the basti is part of the city. The ancesters of Imran Khan’s mother belonging to Burki tribe had also migrated to Jallandhar with this heikh Darvesh. However , the locality or colony still has the same name of "Basti Sheikh"

Initially the Ormur-Guys of Bekai tribe sold some land to Malak Dinis where they built a few huts in early 1950's. Later on they gradually extended their occupation to the area around and built eight permanent houses in the joint property belonging to the whole of Bekai Tribe. When the Bekai tribe tried to stop them from further expansion, the Malak Dins resorted to forcable occupation of the whole Tannuk valley. In this battle two men from Malak Din sid e also got killed and several others injured. It was for the first time during this battle that the Malak Dins realized their defeat seeing the resolve of Burkis under the able leadership of Malik Qarib who were ready to sacrifice their lives in defence of each inch of their ancestor’s land. It is called " Ghojera " in Pashto and " Beshu " in Chitrali. It is a beautiful plant or tree and sprouts a beautiful yellow flower in spring. The name of ‘light- yellow color’ "smeez rang zyaerh" in Ormuri is after this flower as against its darker counterpart "ku rang zyaerh" for orange color. In Waziristan the best of Smeez is grown in Kanigram and the area around it. It s stem and stalk are pretty in a rous ing light s ilver color cotrary to the dark brownish color in other areas. There is asaying in Waziri accent of Pashto that all areas where "Speen Ghojera " is grown used to belong to Ormurs in the past before coming of Wazirs and Mahsuds in the area now called Waziristan

شروع ہوئی اور صرف جرانیوں کے کھیتوں کے فصلوں کو تباہ کیا۔ تذکرۃ الا نصار میں اس طرح کے اور بھی بے شمار واقعات درج ہیں۔ شیخ میاں پیر ولی بدھ کے دن، چھ شعبان 1025 کو کانیگرام میں وفات پاگئے۔ پسماندگاں میں اوروں کے علاوہ اپنا بھتیجا مشہور بزرگ حضرت شیخ درویش کو بھی سوگوار چھوڑا۔ Mian Pir Wali is commonly known with the single syllable name of "Mian" and his mausoleum is situated to the south of Kanigram on the ridge of a thickly grown holly oak trees known with the same name of "Mian Jungle" just across the Rammandsar (Ba dar) rivulet. The jungle is famous for centuries old holly oak trees. It used to be called the "Jewel of Kanigram" due to the evergreen trees giving a very panoramic look from the town. The town dwellers would start their day with opening their eyes to the lush green garden of Mian Sahib. Those ladies and gents who would pass through this jungle on the way to the woods ahead to bring home wooden fuel either on their heads or on the back of their donkeys would feel the pleasure of hearing melodious songs of colourful birds seen there in the early hours of summer mornings. The sight of green fields and the smooth flow of Rammand'sar revolute in between the jungle and the town would make the environment even more romantic and mesmerizing. The jungle had the natural protection through century's old fable that those who would dare cut its trees would face the wrath of Mian Sahib and would surely suffer from some disability. The fable or the myth was not totally improbable as there were instances of casualties happened against those who violated the prohibition. One such incident befell on one Akhmad Zargar who fell down the tree which he was cutting and broke his femur bone in mid-seventies . Even if the reason of this event is not taken as the outcome of this notion, history is witness to many such fateful disasters against those who invited the wrath of nature by violating its laws. Anyway Akhmad's wounds also proved to be fatal and he died a miserable death after protracted illness of about three years. His death was attributed to the curses made by Mian Pir Wali for violation of centuries old practice. If it is so, may Allah Almighty forgive his wrongdoing and rest his soul in peace. However, dry standing and fallen trees were allowed cutting down by the prayer performers who would burn the wood to provide heat to the mosque hujras in the snowy winter days of the town. Shaikhul Azam Mian Pirwali ibne Sheikh Rahimdad, ibne Sheikh Allahdad, ibne Sheikh Ibrahim, ibne Sheikh Bayazid (Baba Shehbaz) was born and brought up in Kaniguram. When young, he joined the service of a rich man called Sher Khan Albarak Bakhtiar in Burhanpur, Ahmadabad but soon after he came to Jullunder to meet his maternal uncle Shaikh Ahmad Ghaus. His uncle advised him to go back to Kanigram and preach the people in accordance with the teachings of Suharvardia school of thought. In Kanigram he enjoyed a good company of friends and apprentices. Soon he became popular as a conciliator to resolve differences between families and tribes. This role won him popularity even beyond Kaniguram among Lohanies (Marwats, Gandapurs and Niazies) who were Baraki's neighbors in Kohistan (Waziristan since 1894) before arrival of Wazirs/Mehsuds at the end of 18th century. One such serious dispute among Lohani Sardars was brought before him and he succeeded in resolving it by personally visiting the rival parties at Tank. Beside these events "Tazkeratul-Ansar" of Ali Mohammad Ansari has narrated many supernatural stories of the saint in his life. One such story is about an incidence when a sudden voice started coming out of the graveyard of Jarani sub-tribe. When the matter was reported to him, he informed the other sheikhs and requested them for joint prayers. After an hour the voice died down and when asked the sheikh about the matter, he stated that a woman was tormented in one of the graves. Another story narrated in the book is that after his death some youngsters of Jarani tribe visited his shrine to pray for rain but since they did not observe the due respect for the shrine what happened was that before their raising, clouds came up and a storm of hailstones caught the crop of only tho se fields which belonged to Jaranis . Many other interesting stories about the life and work of saint Pirwali and others have been ment ioned in the book in such a conviction tha t they ostensibly seem factual. He departed from this world on Wednesday 06, Shaban 1025 AD and buried the next day in this place shown in the picture. He left behind among the bereaved, his nephew the famous Sheikh Da rveh.

He is said to have the power of just calling wild rams. He would select one or more among many present in response to his call. He would slaughter that and offer dishes of its meat to the guests coming from far flung areas to see the saint. He would preserve its stags in this shrine which is now his burial place too. Thousands of such trophies were lying secure till very recently in the shape of a wall-stock as is evident from the picture taken as late as in May, 1983. Unfortunately this precious treasury in the shrine was burned by the Taliban in 2007 holding their preservation unIslamic despite the fact that the two horns of the lamb from Paradise the prophet Ibrahim (peace be upon him) had slaughtered instead of Ismail (peace be upon him) hung on the Ka^bah for the people to see for many hundreds of years. They were still there when Prophet Muhammad lived, and continued to be there until the ruler-ship of Abdullah Ibnuz-Zubayr. At that time the Blessed House was set on fire by the unjust. These two horns burned in that fire.

ارمڑی ورکشاپ: یہ ارمڑی زبان پر تاریخ کی پہلی ورکشاپ تھی جو 4نومبر 2019 کوگورنمنٹ ہائی سکول کانی گرام میں منعقد کی گئی جس میں ارمڑی الف ب کو روزی خان برکی نے خود بڑی تفصیل سے سمجھائیں۔ اس سے ایک دن پہلے ڈیرہ اسماعیل خان میں نیشنل ارمڑی کانفرنس منعقد کی گئی جس میں بڑی تعداد میں ماہرین نے حصہ لیا اور ارمڑی زبان کو معدوم ہونے سے بچانے کے لئے مقالے پڑے۔ اسی کانفرنس میں روزی خان برکی کی ارمڑی زبان پر لکھنے والی ساری کتابوں بشمول ان کا شعری مجموعہ "گپی نر گلی" (پتھر میں پھول) کی بھی رونمائی کی گئی Ormuri workshop: This was the first ever workshop on Ormuri Language held in Government High School Kanigram on 4th of November, 2019 wherein Rozi Khan Burki personally explained the Ormuri Orthography and the Alphabets created by him and duly approved and sponsored by the KP government. A day before a National Ormuri Conference was held in D. I. Khan and attended by a large number of linguists and language activists. They spoke about the challenges of survival faced by Ormuri on the eve of its speakers forced to leave the area for seven long years due to war on terror. In this conference Rozi Khan Burki presented his books written on Ormuri including his poetry collection "Flowers in Stones" published the same year.
